headline: Iambic Therapeutics has applied to the FDA to start human trials of IAM217, a cancer drug candidate it says its AI platform designed.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a company-announced trial filing for an AI-designed drug, early and untested in people.
importance_line: Patients with aggressive, hard-to-treat cancers, including tumors that spread to the brain, are the eventual target, but the evidence so far is the company's own preclinical data, the drug has not been tested in people, and FDA clearance of the trial is still pending.
source: Iambic Therapeutics, in a press release carried by Business Wire
summary: Iambic Therapeutics, a San Diego company that uses AI to design drugs, said in a Business Wire press release that it has submitted an Investigational New Drug application, the filing needed before human testing can begin, for IAM217, a candidate meant to block a cell-division protein called KIF18A in cancers such as triple-negative breast and ovarian cancer. The company says the drug is believed to reach the brain and shrank established brain tumors by about 90% in a preclinical model, but it has not yet been tested in people and the FDA has yet to clear the trial.
notes: Business Wire page blocked here (HTTP 000); the same release text was read on the company's site: https://www.iambic.ai/post/iambic-submits-ind-for-a-potentially-brain-penetrant-kif18a-inhibitor-iam217-its-second-wholly-owned-ai-discovered-candidate . AI-design claim, IND submission and the 90% result are the company's own statements.
